summary: DirScanCache (internal/loaders/dircache.go) snapshots directory-loader output keyed on the canonical root plus a per-file signature (relative path, size, nanosecond modification time) and is wired into LoadToolData for every directory scanner (Claude, codewhale, Droid, command-code, Agy, Grok, DeepSeek (DSH)). An untouched tree is served without re-reading file bodies; any add/remove/change forces a full rescan. Measured at revision 78b5d70: large-fixture warm p50 42.4ms -> 5.5ms (n=20, PASS within the 10ms budget), small-fixture warm p50 7.8ms -> 5.9ms (n=100), cold latency unchanged (11.6ms p50, cache reset per cold sample), and live freshness preserved (81ms at 100ms, 886ms at 1s). Tests cover append/rewrite/truncate/delete, corrupt cache, loader errors, warning round-trips, and cache-vs-full-scan deep equality; AGENTS.md rule 2.A.4 documents the cache and its stat-based boundary.

cases.evidence: TestDirScanCacheGenericWrapper proves the loader body is not re-run for an unchanged tree (call counter stays at 1) and that cached results deep-equal the first load including warnings. TestDirScanCacheClaudeIntegration verifies cached views equal a forced full scan after every mutation and that a cached read stays under 250ms on the test fixture.

TestDirScanCacheClaudeIntegration walks append (+1500), rewrite, truncate, and delete with exact totals; TestDirectoryScanSignature covers add/rewrite/truncate/delete at the signature level and documents the same-size same-mtime boundary. Corrupt cache JSON and a failing loader both fall back to a full scan without poisoning the snapshot.

./scripts/benchmark.sh at 78b5d70 exited 0: baseline exact (1,873,500) and five delta cases exact before any timing; warm p50 5.9ms (n=100) and 5.5ms (n=20) both PASS vs the previous 7.8ms/42.4ms; live CPU 1.08%/0.46% with freshness 81ms/886ms and cancellation <=2ms.
